title: scikit-learn User Guide
summary: The practical guide to classical machine learning with scikit-learn.
description: Covers supervised and unsupervised learning, model selection, preprocessing, pipelines, and evaluation with consistent examples. The user guide is the fastest way to move from a dataset to a defensible baseline.

title: PyTorch Tutorials
summary: Hands-on PyTorch tutorials from tensors and autograd to training and deployment.
description: Official tutorials that build models step by step, including vision, text, reinforcement learning, and distributed training. Each lesson is runnable and links to the underlying API docs.

title: TensorFlow Guides
summary: Official TensorFlow guides for tensors, Keras models, training loops, and deployment.
description: A structured path through the TensorFlow ecosystem, from basic tensors and Keras to custom training loops and SavedModel export. Useful when you need the framework's production tooling.

title: Hugging Face Transformers
summary: The reference for pretrained transformer models, tokenizers, pipelines, and fine-tuning.
description: Documents the Transformers library across text, vision, audio, and multimodal models. The task guides and model pages make it practical to load a checkpoint, run inference, and adapt it to your data.

title: Hugging Face LLM Course
summary: A free, chapter-by-chapter course on transformers and modern LLM workflows.
description: Starts with pipelines and tokenizers, then moves through fine-tuning, sharing models, and task-specific workflows. The notebooks and exercises make it a strong bridge from theory to working code.

title: OpenAI Cookbook
summary: Runnable recipes for prompts, embeddings, RAG, agents, and evaluation with OpenAI APIs.
description: A maintained collection of notebooks and examples that show how to structure real LLM applications. Useful for copying proven patterns for retrieval, tool calling, structured outputs, and evals.

title: LangChain Documentation
summary: The Python guide to composing LLM apps, tools, memory, and retrieval chains.
description: Covers model integrations, prompt templates, retrievers, agents, and evaluation. The tutorials provide end-to-end examples, while the how-to guides are easier to use as a reference once the basics are clear.

title: LlamaIndex Documentation
summary: A framework guide for indexing private data and building retrieval-augmented LLM apps.
description: Documents loaders, node parsing, indexes, retrievers, query engines, and agent workflows. The examples focus on connecting your own data to an LLM with controllable retrieval and citations.

title: LangGraph
summary: Build stateful, multi-step LLM agents as graphs with explicit control flow.
description: LangGraph documents how to model agents as nodes and edges, persist state, add human review, and handle long-running workflows. It is a better fit than a simple chain when the control flow matters.

title: MCP Python SDK
summary: The official Python SDK for building Model Context Protocol servers and clients.
description: Provides the building blocks for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to MCP-compatible clients. The examples cover local servers, transports, and integration with agent frameworks.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK
summary: A lightweight Python SDK for tool-using agents, handoffs, and traced workflows.
description: OpenAI's Agents SDK provides primitives for agent loops, function tools, guardrails, sessions, and observability. The examples are compact enough to adapt into a first production prototype.

title: Ollama
summary: Run open models locally with a simple CLI and a local API for Python.
description: Ollama downloads and serves models such as Llama, Qwen, and Mistral on your own machine. The local API and Python examples make it a practical starting point for offline experiments and privacy-sensitive prototypes.

title: Chroma Documentation
summary: An open-source vector database for embeddings, metadata filtering, and RAG.
description: Chroma's docs cover collections, embedding functions, queries, and persistence. The Python-first API is small enough to add semantic search to a prototype without operating a separate service.

title: Qdrant Documentation
summary: A production-oriented vector search guide covering collections, filtering, and hybrid search.
description: Qdrant documents payload indexes, filtering, quantization, snapshots, and deployment options. Useful once a prototype needs scalable vector search with richer metadata constraints.

title: LLMs from Scratch
summary: Build a GPT-style language model from first principles, one chapter at a time.
description: Sebastian Raschka's book code walks through tokenization, attention, training, fine-tuning, and evaluation in PyTorch. The notebook-first structure makes the internals concrete without hiding the math.

title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
summary: Andrej Karpathy's video series on neural networks, backpropagation, and language models.
description: A companion page for the Zero to Hero series, which builds up from micrograd and makemore to a small GPT. The videos are long but reward careful note-taking and hands-on repetition.
